title: Orbit Shelf contextual workspace switcher & adaptive sidebar prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a new compact, context-aware workspace switcher called "Orbit Shelf" and an adaptive sidebar pattern that surfaces task-relevant tools and cost lenses based on route and user role. The goal is to reduce workspace-switch friction, improve discoverability of rollouts/dashboards, and surface cost/latency signals without overwhelming the primary work surface.
background: Current console navigation is a long vertical rail with a static workspace switcher and a catch-all sidebar. Feedback from platform teams shows: frequent accidental workspace switches, hidden rollout controls, and poor visibility for cost diagnostics. Research sessions (Dec 2024 - Jan 2025) found that engineers want faster switching plus an in-context view of cost/latency for active routes.
goals: Reduce average time to switch workspaces from ~6s to <2s in prototype flows
Surface rollout controls and cost indicators within two clicks of relevant dashboards
Provide an adaptive sidebar that reduces clutter by showing only relevant toolsets per route and user role
constraints: Must work within existing top-level auth & RBAC model
Needs to degrade gracefully for small screens and for users with many workspaces
Implementation must not require new backend endpoints for initial MVP (use existing workspace metadata and route hints)
design_proposal: Orbit Shelf is a horizontal collapsible shelf anchored below the top nav. On hover/expand it shows recent and pinned workspaces, plus a contextual quick-actions area (e.g., 'open rollout', 'view cost lens', 'jump to logs'). The adaptive sidebar will use route-scoped affordances: dashboards show metric cards and cost summary; rollout routes show canary controls and diff links; model endpoints show latency histogram and token-cost estimate. Visual language emphasizes lightweight cards, micro-animations for switching, and a persistent small cost chip next to route titles.
user_research_findings: In moderated tasks 9/12 participants completed a workspace switch in <3s with the shelf vs 6/12 with baseline
Participants valued an inline cost chip; most used it as a tiebreaker when choosing model variants
Some users wanted explicit 'restore previous workspace' action after accidental switches
design_decisions: Choose horizontal shelf over updated vertical switcher to avoid increasing rail height
Show only top 6 recent/pinned workspaces in primary shelf; 'More' opens a full selector to avoid overpopulating
Cost chip is shown by default for routes with >$0.05/min estimated spend; user can collapse it in preferences
engineering_feedback: Continuous-batching team: prefer that quick-action calls reuse existing route params to avoid new API surface
Runtime infra: want a feature flag gate for the adaptive sidebar rollout to limit exposure and A/B test impact
Frontend: animation budget must be limited to preserve 60fps on lower-end devices
accessibility_notes: Shelf is keyboard-navigable with arrow keys and supports screenreader labels for actions
Color contrast updated for cost chip to meet WCAG AA
Provide reduced-motion alternative in account settings

open_questions: Should the shelf show cross-workspace dependencies (e.g., linked dashboards) or keep strictly per-workspace?
How should the shelf behave for accounts with >200 workspaces? Pagination? Search?
What telemetry signals should be used to measure rollout success beyond click-through (e.g., task completion, error rate)
acceptance_criteria: Orbit Shelf prototype implemented behind feature flag and deployed to staging
Keyboard accessibility passes manual QA and automated Lighthouse checks
Telemetry tracks: shelf open rate, workspace switch latency, cost-chip interactions
A/B canary: target orgs show no >1% regression in task completion or error rates after 2 weeks
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Users with many workspaces may not find their target quickly. Mitigation: include search-as-you-type and 'recent first' heuristics
Risk: Cost chip could create anxiety or clutter. Mitigation: default collapse threshold and user preference to hide chips
Risk: Frontend perf regressions from micro-animations. Mitigation: opt-in reduced motion and animation frame budget
